name: Ploutos Money
rootCause: The Ploutos protocol (an Aave v3 fork) on Ethereum suffered a $390K loss due to a single misconfigured Chainlink price feed in its lending pool (0xD060EbD4f56bE8866376a3616B6e5aEF87F945D2). A configuration transaction in block 24538896 mistakenly assigned the BTC/USD Chainlink oracle to price USDC, causing the protocol to treat each USDC as worth tens of thousands of dollars. An attacker — who was either monitoring the mempool or may have had insider knowledge — acted in the immediately following block (24538897), depositing only 8 USDC as collateral and borrowing approximately 187 ETH (~$390K) before the oracle could be corrected. The protocol's website and X account were subsequently scrubbed, raising strong suspicions of a planned exit rather than a purely opportunistic external exploit. Attack Tx: 0xa17dc37e1b65c65d20042212fb834974f7faaa961442e3fc05393778705f8474 Analysis: BlockSec Phalcon — Ploutos Oracle Misconfiguration Alert

The DeFi lending protocol Ploutos Money suffered an exploit due to a misconfigured price oracle (using Chainlink’s BTC/USD feed for USDC price), allowing an attacker to deposit minimal USDC collateral and borrow ~187.36 ETH, draining approximately $390K. The project’s website and social accounts were deleted shortly after, raising strong suspicions of an inside job or exit scam.

On February 26, 2026, Ploutos Money suffered a $390,000 loss on Ethereum after its lending protocol mapped the USDC collateral asset to a BTC/USD price feed. This misconfiguration let an attacker deposit less than 9 USDC and borrow nearly all protocol ETH liquidity, draining the lending pool in a single exploit. Ploutos Money's lending pool mapped its USDC collateral to a BTC/USD Chainlink oracle instead of a stablecoin-appropriate feed, causing massive overvaluation of USDC collateral and enabling catastrophic undercollateralized borrowing.
